page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical ARM64 cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and includes a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, though it lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU physics tests all scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, achieving top-tier ratings in both cached read-only and uncached large-block read/write operations. Single-core performance is moderately strong, placing in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core and the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests.

While the server excels in multi-threaded tasks, database operations, and Redis SET operations, it exhibits some performance tradeoffs. Specifically, LLM text generation for small 135M models falls into the bottom 25%, whereas text generation for larger 7B and 70B models reaches top-tier speeds. Given the high memory density and strong multi-core throughput, this instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, Redis deployments, and multi-threaded software compilation.
